reasoning: The only disagreement centers on rollup.config.mjs, where qwen flagged a build-time fetch from releases.rocket.chat as unsafe. This is a false positive: (1) the domain is Rocket.Chat's own upstream infrastructure, not an unrelated third party; (2) the fetched content is a JWT, which is self-authenticating by design (the 'signed' field qwen noted IS the signature); (3) this file is part of the upstream source tarball, not code injected by the AUR maintainer. The escalation audit correctly identified these facts. All other reviewed files (PKGBUILD, .install, build scripts, wrapper.sh, etc.) are standard Electron packaging tooling with no injection patterns.
disagreement_analysis: Qwen overreacted to a legitimate build-time network fetch. It failed to recognize that releases.rocket.chat is the package's own upstream domain (the package has a stated relationship with it), and failed to understand that JWTs provide their own integrity verification. It also didn't apply the key test: this is upstream code in the source tarball, not something the AUR maintainer could have injected. The escalation audit (claude-sonnet-4.6) correctly resolved this by identifying the domain ownership and JWT self-authentication.
coverage_issues: deepseek-deepseek-v4-flash failed with a tool error (crash during clone) - no verdict signal
Neither model reviewed the full yarn.lock or all node_modules resolution paths, but this is acceptable since npm dependency resolution is a known hygiene concern, not an injection vector
false_positives: rollup.config.mjs 'Downloads unverified remote content during build' - FP because: (1) fetches from project's own infrastructure (releases.rocket.chat), (2) content is a JWT which is self-authenticating, (3) this is upstream code not AUR-maintainer injection, (4) serves legitimate purpose of fetching version metadata
learnings: Models need better context about upstream project infrastructure - when a fetch goes to a domain that is clearly the project's own (e.g., releases.<project>.chat for a <project> package), this should not be flagged as suspicious
Models should recognize JWTs as self-authenticating content - the presence of a 'signed' field in a JWT response is evidence OF integrity verification, not lack thereof

The distinction between 'upstream code in source tarball' vs 'AUR maintainer injection' needs stronger emphasis - build scripts that come from the upstream tarball cannot be injected by the AUR maintainer

Network fetches during build from the project's own infrastructure for legitimate metadata (version lists, supported versions) are normal patterns and should not trigger unsafe verdicts without evidence of host mismatch or purpose mismatch
